scope: Read the complete Japanese article and all twelve translations. Compared taxonomy, threats, output encoding/CSP/HttpOnly, CSRF assumptions and token patterns, SameSite scope and limitations, code examples, diagram, and references with official OWASP cheat sheets and MDN.
findings: All editions preserve the distinction between executing script in the same-origin browser context (XSS) and inducing cookie-authenticated cross-site requests (CSRF).
The article limits the form attack to a SameSite=None; Secure scenario without token or Origin checks and notes that browser third-party-cookie controls can block it.
The naive Double Submit equality check is identified as insufficient when cookie injection is possible; the signed, session-bound HMAC form is recommended.
CSP is explicitly an additional layer; SameSite and HttpOnly are not presented as substitutes for application-level protections.
All snippets, diagram structure, and six official references match across languages; no material translation discrepancy requiring correction was found.
publicationStatus: Re-review only; no source or translation content changed, so no deployment was required.
